scoring.partial: Partially implemented or has known issues

overall.assessment: Strong CI/CD foundation and documentation are the project's main strengths. Primary gaps are in observability (no structured logging), security scanning breadth (gosec, CodeQL), developer experience tooling (golangci-lint, devcontainer), and release hardening (SBOM, SLSA, binary signing). Several interface/type mismatches between server and runner packages need attention.

domains.name: Code Quality & Style
domains.description: Go formatting, linting, static analysis, and code conventions

pillars.name: gofmt compliance
pillars.rationale: CI enforces gofmt -l check on every push/PR. Fails on non-conformant files.

pillars.name: go vet pass
pillars.rationale: go vet ./... runs in CI as part of the ci.yml workflow. No known vet warnings.

pillars.name: staticcheck integration
pillars.rationale: staticcheck runs in audit.yml with honnef.co/go/tools/cmd/staticcheck@latest.

pillars.name: golangci-lint configuration
pillars.rationale: No .golangci.yml or .golangci.yaml in repo. golangci-lint is the de facto Go meta-linter and should replace/adjoin the ad-hoc staticcheck step.
pillars.remediation: Add .golangci.yml with enabled linters: errcheck, gosimple, ineffassign, unused, staticcheck, gosec, revive, exportloopref. Integrate into CI and Makefile.

pillars.name: compiler warnings (zero tolerance)
pillars.rationale: Go 1.25 enforces zero warnings on build. No known compiler warnings.

pillars.name: receiver naming consistency
pillars.rationale: Codebase uses consistent single-letter or short receivers (r *Runner, s *Server, h *ResultHistory).

pillars.name: import ordering (stdlib / external / internal)
pillars.rationale: Most files follow Go convention (stdlib, then external, then internal) but no tool enforces it. goimports not in CI.
pillars.remediation: Add goimports -local kwatch check to CI or enable in golangci-lint.

pillars.name: package documentation comments
pillars.rationale: Some packages have doc comments (runner, server) but others like cmd, tui, security lack package-level doc.
pillars.remediation: Add package-level doc comments to cmd/, tui/, security/, config/, mcp/ packages.

pillars.name: exported symbol documentation
pillars.rationale: Many exported types and functions have comments (NewRunner, New, StartWithContext) but some are missing (e.g., FormatCompactStatus, getCommandType).
pillars.remediation: Audit all exported symbols with golint or revive and add missing doc comments.

pillars.name: cyclomatic complexity management
pillars.rationale: No complexity gate in CI or local tooling. Some functions (e.g., cmd_test.go at 1306 lines) are excessively large.
pillars.remediation: Add gocyclo or revive cyclomatic check to golangci-lint, target max 15. Refactor large test file.

pillars.name: function length discipline
pillars.rationale: Most functions are reasonably sized but server.setupRoutes() and cmd.run.go's Execute() are overly long. cmd/cmd_test.go is 1306 lines.
pillars.remediation: Split setupRoutes into route registration + middleware assembly. Break up cmd_test.go into focused test files.

pillars.name: error string conventions
pillars.rationale: Error strings follow Go convention (lowercase, no trailing punctuation) in most places.

pillars.name: nil slice handling
pillars.rationale: Codebase correctly uses var declarations and make() for slices. No nil-append patterns found.

pillars.name: commented-out code removal
pillars.rationale: Some commented-out code blocks exist in cmd/ and runner/. Not excessive but should be cleaned.
pillars.remediation: Remove dead commented-out code. Use git history for reference.

pillars.name: consistent constructor pattern
pillars.rationale: New* constructors consistently return pointers and take config structs. E.g., NewRunner(), New(), NewParser().

pillars.name: enum/const naming conventions
pillars.rationale: CommandType constants use PascalCase with clear suffixes (TypescriptCheck, LintCheck, TestRunner).

pillars.name: var vs := consistency
pillars.rationale: Codebase appropriately uses both var and := declarations in Go-idiomatic fashion.

pillars.name: context usage correctness
pillars.rationale: Runner correctly passes context.Context for command timeouts. But server/types.go Runner interface uses context.Context as interface{} in signature — type mismatch with actual runner.Runner.
pillars.remediation: Fix server/types.go Runner interface to use context.Context instead of interface{}, and align return types with runner.Runner.

domains.name: Testing & Reliability
domains.description: Test coverage, types, tooling, and quality practices

pillars.name: go test pass rate
pillars.rationale: CI runs go test ./... on every push/PR. All tests passing.

pillars.name: table-driven tests
pillars.rationale: Some test files use table-driven patterns (config_test.go, runner_test.go). Others use sequential test functions without subtables.
pillars.remediation: Convert sequential tests in security/ and tui/ to table-driven style where appropriate.

pillars.name: test coverage CI gate
pillars.rationale: Makefile has test-coverage target (go test -cover) but coverage is not gated in CI. No coverage threshold or reporting.
pillars.remediation: Add go test -coverprofile=coverage.out to CI, enforce minimum 60% coverage gate per package. Add Codecov or coveralls integration.

pillars.name: fuzz testing
pillars.rationale: No Go fuzz targets (*_test.go with Fuzz* functions) exist. No fuzz testing in CI.
pillars.remediation: Add fuzz targets for parser functions (ParseTestOutput, ParseLintOutput) and config parsing. Add CI fuzz step with -fuzztime=30s.

pillars.name: benchmark testing
pillars.rationale: No benchmark functions (Benchmark*) exist in the codebase. No benchstat or bench CI.
pillars.remediation: Add benchmarks for hot paths: command execution, output parsing, compact status formatting. Add bench CI comparison.

pillars.name: race detector in CI
pillars.rationale: Makefile has dev build with -race flag. CI does not run go test -race. Potential races undetected in automated testing.
pillars.remediation: Add go test -race ./... to CI pipeline as a dedicated step.

pillars.name: integration tests
pillars.rationale: watch_loop_integration_test.go exists (494 lines) but tests are tightly coupled to file system. No hermetic integration test pattern.
pillars.remediation: Refactor integration tests to use temp directories and controlled file events. Add integration test CI job.

pillars.name: hermetic test data
pillars.rationale: Test output parsing tests use inline strings. Watch integration test depends on real filesystem. No testdata/ directory.
pillars.remediation: Create testdata/ directory with fixture files. Use testutil package for temp directory helpers.

pillars.name: test helper utilities
pillars.rationale: No shared test helpers or testutil package. Test setup code is duplicated across test files.
pillars.remediation: Create internal/testutil package with helpers, temp dir creation, mock runners, and common assertions.

pillars.name: mock/stub usage
pillars.rationale: No mock implementations for testing. The Runner interface in server/types.go has no mock. Tests use real command execution.
pillars.remediation: Create mock implementations of Runner interface. Use them in server and tui tests to avoid real command dependency.

pillars.name: parallel test execution
pillars.rationale: No t.Parallel() calls in any test file. Tests run sequentially.
pillars.remediation: Add t.Parallel() to independent test functions. Ensure test isolation before enabling.

pillars.name: test cleanup with t.Cleanup
pillars.rationale: No use of t.Cleanup() for resource cleanup. Manual cleanup is used but inconsistent.
pillars.remediation: Replace manual deferred cleanup with t.Cleanup() in tests that create temp resources.

pillars.name: subtests naming
pillars.rationale: Some test files use named subtests, others use flat function names without t.Run.
pillars.remediation: Adopt consistent subtest naming: all test functions should use t.Run with descriptive names.

pillars.name: test error messages
pillars.rationale: Many tests use t.Errorf/t.Fatalf with descriptive messages. Some use generic messages lacking expected/actual values.
pillars.remediation: Add structured test assertions with want/got format. Consider testify/require for richer assertions.

pillars.name: test file organization
pillars.rationale: cmd/cmd_test.go is 1306 lines — too large for a single file. Should be split by command.
pillars.remediation: Split cmd_test.go into focused per-command test files.

pillars.name: coverage reporting
pillars.rationale: No coverage HTML output, no Codecov/Coveralls, no coverage badge in README.
pillars.remediation: Add go test -coverprofile=coverage.out && go tool cover -html=coverage.out to Makefile. Integrate Codecov.

pillars.name: golden file tests
pillars.rationale: No golden file (*.golden) pattern used. Compact status format and output parsing are tested inline.
pillars.remediation: Use go-cmp and golden files for testing complex output formatting. Particularly useful for FormatCompactStatus.

pillars.name: interface compliance tests
pillars.rationale: server.Runner interface expects different signatures than runner.Runner provides. No compile-time interface satisfaction checks.
pillars.remediation: Add var _ server.Runner = (*runner.Runner)(nil) in test or server package. Fix interface signature mismatch.

domains.name: Dependency Management
domains.description: Go module hygiene, dependency auditing, and supply chain security

pillars.name: go.sum integrity
pillars.rationale: go.sum exists and is checked into VCS. Provides checksum verification for all direct and transitive deps.

pillars.name: go mod tidy run
pillars.rationale: go mod tidy runs periodically (Makefile deps target). Module is clean.

pillars.name: go mod verify
pillars.rationale: deny.yml workflow runs go mod verify to check module integrity against go.sum.

pillars.name: dependency pinning (SHA pinning)
pillars.rationale: All direct deps are pinned to specific versions (v1.3.10, v1.1.0, v1.10.1, etc.). No floating tags.

pillars.name: license allowlist
pillars.rationale: deny.yml runs go-licenses check with allowlist: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3, ISC, MPL-2.0. Non-compliant deps fail CI.

pillars.name: Dependabot configuration
pillars.rationale: dependabot.yml exists with weekly cadence for Go module updates.

pillars.name: automated vulnerability scanning
pillars.rationale: govulncheck runs in CI on push/PR + weekly cron. Scans Go vulnerability database at source level.

pillars.name: dependency freshness tracking
pillars.rationale: Dependabot handles updates but no tool provides freshness dashboard. Some indirect deps are outdated.
pillars.remediation: Consider running go-mod-upgrade periodically or using renovate for more granular dep control.

pillars.name: transitive dependency minimization
pillars.rationale: 12 indirect deps is reasonable for a TUI tool. No unnecessary transitive deps detected.
pillars.remediation: Periodically audit with go mod why and go mod graph to detect bloat.

pillars.name: vendor directory management
pillars.rationale: No vendor/ directory. go.sum-based verification is sufficient for this project size.

pillars.name: replace directive justification
pillars.rationale: No replace directives in go.mod. Not needed for current dependency set.

pillars.name: indirect dependency documentation
pillars.rationale: go.mod clearly separates direct and indirect deps with // indirect comments. Standard Go tooling format.

pillars.name: Go toolchain version policy
pillars.rationale: go.mod specifies go 1.25.0. CI uses matching 1.25 setup step in ci.yml and audit.yml.

pillars.name: deny.toml relevance
pillars.rationale: deny.toml at root is a dormant Rust cargo-deny config, not applicable to Go project. Creates confusion.
pillars.remediation: Remove deny.toml (Rust config in Go project). It has no effect and misleads contributors.

pillars.name: private module configuration
pillars.rationale: No private module dependencies. GOPROXY/GONOSUMCHECK config not needed.

domains.name: Security
domains.description: SAST, DAST, secret scanning, supply chain security, and secure coding practices

pillars.name: govulncheck integration
pillars.rationale: Runs in audit.yml on push/PR + weekly cron. Source-mode scan traces call graph. Fails on any known vulnerability.

pillars.name: gosec static analysis
pillars.rationale: No gosec scan in CI or local tooling. gosec is the standard Go security linter.
pillars.remediation: Add gosec to audit.yml. Or enable its rules via golangci-lint which has a gosec linter wrapper.

pillars.name: CodeQL analysis
pillars.rationale: No CodeQL workflow. Standard GitHub security analysis for Go projects is absent.
pillars.remediation: Add github/codeql-action with go queries to audit.yml or a new codeql.yml. Schedule weekly.

pillars.name: gitleaks secret scanning
pillars.rationale: gitleaks runs in audit.yml with fetch-depth:0 for full git history scan. SARIF upload available.

pillars.name: Trivy filesystem scan
pillars.rationale: Trivy runs in audit.yml on every push/PR + weekly. Scan type: fs. SARIF upload with security-events:write.

pillars.name: .gitleaks.toml existence
pillars.rationale: .gitleaks.toml exists at root with custom allowlist rules. Referenced by gitleaks-action config-path.

pillars.name: SLSA provenance
pillars.rationale: No SLSA-generator workflow. Release artifacts are not signed or attested.
pillars.remediation: Add SLSA-generator step to release.yml. Generate non-forgeable provenance attestation for release artifacts.

pillars.name: SBOM generation
pillars.rationale: No SPDX or CycloneDX SBOM generated during build or release.
pillars.remediation: Add CycloneDX SBOM generation to release.yml (using cyclonedx-gomod or syft). Attach to GitHub Release.

pillars.name: built-in secret scanner (Go code)
pillars.rationale: security/ package has 20+ regex patterns for secret detection. Provides /security/scan, /security/findings APIs.

pillars.name: security API endpoints
pillars.rationale: Security endpoints: /security/scan, /security/findings, /security/resolve/:id, /security/ignore/:id.

pillars.name: input validation (type-safe)
pillars.rationale: Go strong typing provides compile-time input validation. Command arguments and config are parsed with validation.

pillars.name: command injection prevention
pillars.rationale: Uses exec.CommandContext with separate command/args arrays (not shell strings). No shell injection vector.

pillars.name: path traversal prevention
pillars.rationale: WorkingDir is constrained to configured directories. No user-supplied path traversal in file operations.

pillars.name: authentication for server endpoints
pillars.rationale: authMiddleware supports AuthToken configuration. Production server constructors enforce auth.

pillars.name: CORS configuration
pillars.rationale: CORS middleware with configurable AllowedOrigins. '*' allowed in dev, restricted in production.

pillars.name: dependency scanning coverage
pillars.rationale: Trivy fs scan covers Go module vulnerabilities in audit.yml. govulncheck covers Go vuln DB.

pillars.name: SAST coverage in CI
pillars.rationale: staticcheck provides Go-specific SAST. Missing gosec and CodeQL for broader analysis.
pillars.remediation: Add gosec via golangci-lint. Add CodeQL Go queries workflow.

pillars.name: secret scanning in git history
pillars.rationale: gitleaks runs with fetch-depth: 0 for full history scan in audit.yml.

pillars.name: HTTP security headers
pillars.rationale: fastResponseMiddleware sets security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, etc.).

pillars.name: binary signing (cosign/GPG)
pillars.rationale: Release artifacts are unsigned. No GPG/cosign signing of binaries or checksums.
pillars.remediation: Add cosign signing of release artifacts and SHA256SUMS file. Publish public key in repo.

domains.name: Observability
domains.description: Structured logging, metrics, tracing, and operational visibility

pillars.name: structured logging (slog)
pillars.rationale: Entire codebase uses fmt.Printf and log.Printf. No structured logging (slog, logrus, zap). JSON-level output, key-value pairs, and log levels absent.
pillars.remediation: Migrate from log.Printf to slog (Go 1.21+ standard library). Add JSON handler option for production. Add request-scoped logging with context.

pillars.name: log levels (debug/info/warn/error)
pillars.rationale: No log level infrastructure. All logging is unconditional log.Printf. Debug logging not available.
pillars.remediation: Add slog with LevelVar for runtime-configurable log level. Wire to CLI --verbose flag.

pillars.name: request-scoped logging
pillars.rationale: logMiddleware logs requests but without structured fields or request IDs.
pillars.remediation: Add request ID middleware. Use slog with request_id, method, path, duration fields.

pillars.name: panic recovery middleware
pillars.rationale: No panic recovery in HTTP middleware. A handler panic would crash the server.
pillars.remediation: Add recovery middleware (outermost) that catches panics, logs stack trace, returns 500.

pillars.name: metrics endpoints
pillars.rationale: /metrics endpoint provides request count, error count, average response time, memory/CPU/goroutines.

pillars.name: health check endpoints
pillars.rationale: /health endpoint with system info (uptime, Go version, directory). /quick for ultra-fast health check.

pillars.name: slow request detection
pillars.rationale: No slow request logging or threshold-based alerting.
pillars.remediation: Add middleware that logs warnings for requests exceeding configurable threshold (e.g., >1s).

pillars.name: error rate monitoring
pillars.rationale: ServerMetrics.ErrorCount exists but is not exposed via endpoint or logging threshold.
pillars.remediation: Surface error_count in /health response. Add warning log when error rate exceeds threshold.

pillars.name: pprof endpoints
pillars.rationale: No pprof endpoints for deep profiling. CPU/memory metrics are basic sampled values.
pillars.remediation: Add net/http/pprof handlers behind a --pprof flag for on-demand profiling.

pillars.name: structured error types
pillars.rationale: No custom error types with error wrapping. Errors are returned as plain strings or fmt.Errorf. No sentinel errors.
pillars.remediation: Define sentinel errors and custom error types with wrapping (%w). Add errors.Is/errors.As support.

pillars.name: audit logging
pillars.rationale: No audit trail of admin actions or API requests with authentication context.
pillars.remediation: Add structured audit log for authenticated API requests. Log to file with rotation.

pillars.name: request/response logging middleware
pillars.rationale: logMiddleware logs method, path, status code, duration. Good basic request observability.

pillars.name: latency tracking (percentiles)
pillars.rationale: Metrics track average response time. No percentile breakdown (p50/p90/p99) or latency histogram.
pillars.remediation: Add latency histogram tracking to metrics. Expose p50/p90/p99 via /metrics endpoint.

pillars.name: structured error responses
pillars.rationale: ErrorResponse type with error, timestamp, code fields. Consistent JSON error format in API.

pillars.name: environment-aware logging
pillars.rationale: No environment-specific log configuration. Dev vs prod logging is identical (log.Printf).
pillars.remediation: Add --log-format flag (text/json) and --log-level flag. Default to text in dev, JSON in production.

domains.name: Release & CI/CD
domains.description: Release pipeline, artifact management, CI hygiene, and distribution

pillars.name: tag-driven releases
pillars.rationale: release.yml triggers on v* tag push. Cross-compiles and publishes GitHub Release.

pillars.name: CI pipeline (build + test)
pillars.rationale: ci.yml runs gofmt, go build, go test, go vet on every push/PR to main + feature branches.

pillars.name: audit pipeline
pillars.rationale: audit.yml runs govulncheck, staticcheck, Trivy, gitleaks on push/PR to main + weekly cron.

pillars.name: release-drafter
pillars.rationale: release-drafter.yml auto-generates release notes on push to main. Draft release created before tag build.

pillars.name: goreleaser automation
pillars.rationale: Release is hand-rolled (cross-compile loop + softprops/action-gh-release). No goreleaser for standardized Go releases.
pillars.remediation: Migrate to goreleaser for standardized Go cross-compilation, artifact naming, Homebrew formula generation, and Docker image publishing.

pillars.name: binary signing
pillars.rationale: No GPG or cosign signing of release binaries or checksum files.
pillars.remediation: Add cosign keyless signing to release.yml. Sign SHA256SUMS and attach signature.

pillars.name: SHA256SUMS generation
pillars.rationale: release.yml generates SHA256SUMS for all release artifacts with sha256sum utility.

pillars.name: cross-compilation
pillars.rationale: Release cross-compiles for 5 targets: linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, windows/amd64.

pillars.name: semantic versioning
pillars.rationale: Tag-driven v* convention. Version extracted from git tag for ldflags injection.

pillars.name: changelog generation
pillars.rationale: CHANGELOG.md auto-generated by git-cliff with cliff.toml config. 49 lines, well-structured.

pillars.name: Docker image publishing
pillars.rationale: Dockerfile exists at root with multi-stage build. Containerized deployment supported.

pillars.name: Homebrew formula
pillars.rationale: No Homebrew tap or formula for macOS distribution.
pillars.remediation: Add Homebrew formula to release pipeline (goreleaser can auto-generate this).

pillars.name: CI concurrency & cancellation
pillars.rationale: ci.yml and audit.yml use concurrency groups with cancel-in-progress: true. Release serializes per-tag without cancellation.

pillars.name: CI timeout bounds
pillars.rationale: All workflows have explicit timeout-minutes (ci: 10, audit: 10, release: 20). Prevents runaway jobs.

pillars.name: CI least-privilege permissions
pillars.rationale: All workflows use top-level permissions: contents: read. Release escalates to contents: write only in release job.

pillars.name: release version correctness
pillars.rationale: release.yml uses go-version: "1.21" but go.mod requires 1.25. Release builds with wrong Go version breaking compilation.
pillars.remediation: Fix release.yml to use go-version: "1.25" matching go.mod. This is a critical bug — release binary build will fail.

pillars.name: staggered cron schedules
pillars.rationale: Audit (Mon 06:00), scorecard (Wed), governance (Mon 06:17) — staggered to avoid CI stacking.

pillars.name: persist-credentials: false
pillars.rationale: All checkout steps use persist-credentials: false. Token hygiene prevents credential leakage.

domains.name: Documentation & Governance
domains.description: Project docs, ADRs, SSOT, community standards, and governance

pillars.name: README completeness
pillars.rationale: 1087-line README with badges, feature overview, installation guide, usage, configuration, API docs, MCP integration, troubleshooting.

pillars.name: ARCHITECTURE.md
pillars.rationale: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md exists with package overview, data flow, and component diagram.

pillars.name: CONTRIBUTING.md
pillars.rationale: 92-line CONTRIBUTING.md with setup, testing, PR guidelines, and code review process.

pillars.name: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
pillars.rationale: Standard Contributor Covenant with reporting email.

pillars.name: SECURITY.md
pillars.rationale: 1306-line SECURITY.md with vulnerability reporting, hardening measures, and security architecture.

pillars.name: SUPPORT.md
pillars.rationale: SUPPORT.md with issue tracker, discussion, security contacts.

pillars.name: CHANGELOG.md
pillars.rationale: git-cliff generated changelog with conventional commit parsing. 49 lines, well structured.

pillars.name: ADRs (Architecture Decision Records)
pillars.rationale: No docs/adr/ directory. No ADRs documenting architectural decisions.
pillars.remediation: Create docs/adr/ directory. Document key decisions: TUI framework choice (bubbletea), cobra CLI, HTTP server design, security architecture.

pillars.name: SSOT.md accuracy
pillars.rationale: SSOT.md at root states 'Built with Cargo' and refers to 'Primary Rust crate'. This is a Go project.
pillars.remediation: Rewrite SSOT.md: change 'Built with: Cargo' to 'Built with: Go', fix code/config patterns, remove Rust references.

pillars.name: CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md
pillars.rationale: Both files exist and provide comprehensive agent guidance.

pillars.name: API documentation
pillars.rationale: README documents all HTTP endpoints with examples. Docs/FAQ.md and docs/OPERATIONS.md provide additional reference.

pillars.name: MCP documentation
pillars.rationale: README has extensive MCP integration section with tool reference, config examples, and AI agent patterns.

pillars.name: configuration documentation
pillars.rationale: README documents all config options with table, YAML examples, and environment-specific configs.

pillars.name: example files
pillars.rationale: examples/ directory with kwatch.yaml, development.yaml, production.yaml config examples.

pillars.name: LICENSE file
pillars.rationale: LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE exist but no root LICENSE file. Without root LICENSE, default copyright law applies.
pillars.remediation: Create root LICENSE file with MIT text. Reference both LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE if dual-licensed.

pillars.name: CITATION.cff
pillars.rationale: CITATION.cff exists with repository metadata for academic citation.

pillars.name: intent/boundary documentation
pillars.rationale: docs/intent/KWatch.md and docs/boundary/KWatch.md exist per Phenotype registry standard.

pillars.name: OPERATIONS.md
pillars.rationale: docs/OPERATIONS.md with deployment, configuration, and operational guidance.

domains.name: Developer Experience (DX)
domains.description: Local development tooling, onboarding, and productivity tooling

pillars.name: devcontainer configuration
pillars.rationale: No .devcontainer/devcontainer.json for containerized development environment.
pillars.remediation: Add devcontainer with Go 1.25, golangci-lint, gopls, and recommended VS Code extensions.

pillars.name: pre-commit hooks
pillars.rationale: .pre-commit-config.yaml exists but pre-commit hooks are not installed by default. No lefthook.yml or husky equivalent.
pillars.remediation: Activate pre-commit hooks in CONTRIBUTING.md setup instructions. Verify pre-commit CI integration.

pillars.name: golangci-lint local config
pillars.rationale: No .golangci.yml. Developers must know which linters to run manually.
pillars.remediation: Create .golangci.yml with recommended Go linters. Add to Makefile as `make lint` target.

pillars.name: Makefile targets
pillars.rationale: Makefile with build, install, test, dev, build-all, clean, test-coverage, package, run targets.

pillars.name: Justfile targets
pillars.rationale: Justfile provides alternative task runner with overlapping/expanded targets.

pillars.name: .editorconfig
pillars.rationale: .editorconfig with gofmt-compatible settings (indent_style=tab, indent_size=4, charset=utf-8).

pillars.name: .gitattributes
pillars.rationale: .gitattributes with Go-specific patterns, line ending normalization, and linguist overrides.

pillars.name: .gitignore quality
pillars.rationale: 149-line .gitignore with comprehensive Go, OS, editor, and tooling patterns.

pillars.name: initial project onboarding
pillars.rationale: README has Quick Install, From Source, and Basic Commands sections. Low barrier to first build.

pillars.name: hot reload development
pillars.rationale: No air, realize, or nodemon-like hot reload for development. Changes require manual rebuild.
pillars.remediation: Add air (cosmtrek/air) config for live-reload development. Add `make dev-watch` target.

pillars.name: debugger support (Delve)
pillars.rationale: No dlv (Delve) configuration, no VS Code launch.json, no Makefile debug target.
pillars.remediation: Add `make debug` target using dlv. Add VS Code launch.json configuration for debugging.

pillars.name: environment variable management
pillars.rationale: No .env.example or .env file. Some configuration is env-var based but undocumented.
pillars.remediation: Create .env.example with all configurable environment variables and their defaults.

pillars.name: Go workspace support
pillars.rationale: Single module project. go.work not needed.

pillars.name: go generate directives
pillars.rationale: No go:generate directives. No code generation for boilerplate or mocks.
pillars.remediation: Add go:generate for mock generation (counterfeiter or mockgen), stringer for enums.

pillars.name: VS Code integration
pillars.rationale: No .vscode/ directory with settings.json, launch.json, extensions.json, or tasks.json.
pillars.remediation: Add .vscode/ with recommended extensions, Go build task, debug configuration, and workspace settings.

domains.name: Architecture & Design
domains.description: Package organization, error handling, interface design, concurrency, and patterns

pillars.name: error wrapping (fmt.Errorf %w)
pillars.rationale: No use of fmt.Errorf with %w for error wrapping. Errors returned as string values without context preservation or unwrapping.
pillars.remediation: Adopt error wrapping: use fmt.Errorf("context: %w", err) for all error returns. Enable errcheck in golangci-lint.

pillars.name: sentinel errors
pillars.rationale: No defined sentinel errors (var ErrNotFound = errors.New("...")). Callers cannot use errors.Is for error matching.
pillars.remediation: Define sentinel errors in each package: ErrInvalidConfig, ErrCommandTimeout, ErrServerClosed, etc.

pillars.name: custom error types with fields
pillars.rationale: No custom error types implementing error interface. No typed errors for different failure modes.
pillars.remediation: Create custom error types (ConfigError, CommandError, ServerError) with additional context fields. errors.As support.

pillars.name: interface segregation
pillars.rationale: server.Runner interface expects RunAll(ctx interface{}) returning map[string]CommandResult while runner.Runner has incompatible signature. Interface misalignment.
pillars.remediation: Fix server.Runner interface to match runner.Runner signatures: use context.Context, align return types.

pillars.name: package organization
pillars.rationale: Clear package layout: cmd/ (CLI), config/, runner/, server/, tui/, security/, mcp/. Each has single responsibility.

pillars.name: separation of concerns
pillars.rationale: Clean separation: CLI (cmd/) orchestrates, runner/ executes, tui/ displays, server/ serves HTTP. Domain boundaries are clear.

pillars.name: context propagation
pillars.rationale: Runner properly accepts context.Context with timeouts. But server.Runner interface uses interface{} — breaks context propagation.
pillars.remediation: Fix server.Runner interface to accept context.Context. Ensure TUI and server pass context with cancellation.

pillars.name: graceful shutdown
pillars.rationale: Server.StartWithContext handles context cancellation with 5s graceful shutdown. Clean teardown of HTTP listener.

pillars.name: dependency injection
pillars.rationale: Server accepts Runner via constructor injection (New(config, runner)). Good. But Runner creates config internally rather than receiving via DI.
pillars.remediation: Make Runner accept dependencies via constructor consistently. Consider using options pattern for optional configuration.

pillars.name: configuration management pattern
pillars.rationale: Config structs with DefaultConfig() functions. Consistent pattern across packages (server.Config, runner.RunnerConfig, config.Config).

pillars.name: command pattern (cobra)
pillars.rationale: Cobra-based command structure with run, status, daemon, config, history, mcp, security subcommands.

pillars.name: TUI/CLI separation
pillars.rationale: TUI (tui/ package) is cleanly separated from CLI (cmd/). Server mode provides HTTP API as alternative to TUI.

pillars.name: concurrency safety
pillars.rationale: sync.RWMutex in ResultHistory, sync.WaitGroup in RunAll, mutex for concurrent map writes. No obvious race conditions.

pillars.name: data race detection
pillars.rationale: Race detector not in CI pipeline. Makefile dev target uses -race but running race-detected tests is a manual step.
pillars.remediation: Add `go test -race ./...` to CI pipeline. Ensure no data races in concurrent test scenarios.

pillars.name: testability of design
pillars.rationale: server.Runner interface makes server testable in theory, but interface mismatch prevents actual mocking. Runner is concrete hard to mock.
pillars.remediation: Fix Runner interface. Add mock implementations. Use interfaces for file system operations to enable hermetic tests.

pillars.name: server factory functions
pillars.rationale: Multiple server constructors for different environments: QuickServer, SecureServer, DevServer, ProductionServer.

pillars.name: code comments quality
pillars.rationale: Code is generally well-commented with function doc strings explaining purpose, parameters, and behavior.

pillars.name: mutex discipline
pillars.rationale: ResultHistory correctly uses RLock/RUnlock for reads and Lock/Unlock for writes. Consistent locking pattern.

domains.name: Infrastructure & Operations
domains.description: Deployment, containerization, monitoring, and operational readiness

pillars.name: Docker support
pillars.rationale: Dockerfile exists with multi-stage build pattern. Containerized deployment is supported and documented.

pillars.name: Dockerfile quality (multi-stage)
pillars.rationale: Multi-stage Dockerfile with build stage and minimal runtime stage. Reduces final image size.

pillars.name: Docker Compose support
pillars.rationale: No docker-compose.yml for orchestrated deployment with dependencies.
pillars.remediation: Add docker-compose.yml with kwatch service, volume mounts for config, and health check configuration.

pillars.name: container health checks
pillars.rationale: Dockerfile lacks HEALTHCHECK instruction. Container orchestrator cannot monitor liveness.
pillars.remediation: Add HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s CMD curl -f http://localhost:3737/health || exit 1 to Dockerfile.

pillars.name: container resource limits
pillars.rationale: No resource limit guidance or Docker Compose resource reservations documented.
pillars.remediation: Document recommended resource limits (CPU/memory) in OPERATIONS.md. Add to docker-compose.yml.

pillars.name: configuration via environment
pillars.rationale: Some configuration is env-based (port, host, auth token). Not all config options are env-configurable.
pillars.remediation: Add environment variable overrides for all config fields. Precedence: CLI flags > env vars > config file > defaults.

pillars.name: TLS/HTTPS support
pillars.rationale: No TLS configuration. Server runs HTTP only. No support for HTTPS or Let's Encrypt.
pillars.remediation: Add TLS support with --cert-file and --key-file flags. Document reverse proxy setup for production TLS.

pillars.name: systemd service file
pillars.rationale: No kwatch.service file for systemd-managed daemon deployment.
pillars.remediation: Create kwatch.service with Type=simple, restart=always, standard systemd hardening options.

pillars.name: log rotation configuration
pillars.rationale: No logrotate config or log file management. Daemon logs to stderr/stdout only.
pillars.remediation: Add logrotate configuration for daemon log files. Document log management in OPERATIONS.md.

pillars.name: Prometheus metrics format
pillars.rationale: /metrics endpoint is custom JSON, not Prometheus-format. Cannot be scraped by standard Prometheus.
pillars.remediation: Add Prometheus /metrics endpoint with Go runtime metrics (process, goroutine, GC stats) or expose via expvar.

pillars.name: readiness probe vs liveness probe
pillars.rationale: /health serves both liveness and readiness. Kubernetes needs separate /ready for traffic routing.
pillars.remediation: Add /ready endpoint that checks runner readiness, watcher status. Document Kubernetes deployment probes.

pillars.name: port configurability
pillars.rationale: Port is configurable via CLI flag (--port), function parameter, and Config struct. Default 3737.

pillars.name: data persistence (history)
pillars.rationale: Command history is in-memory only. No persistence across restarts. History lost on process exit.
pillars.remediation: Add optional SQLite persistence for command history using modernc.org/sqlite. Add --persist flag.

pillars.name: version information
pillars.rationale: Version injected via ldflags (-X main.version, main.commit, main.buildTime). ServerInfo in API response includes version.
